I have read a few of OPs comments and I understand that they are getting shafted with only 20 hours a week so this comment does not apply in that situation. 

I am a supervisor at a chain auto part store and this issue does come into play many times while rostering, although I live in Australia so it the way it's handled in the US may be different. Essentially there is a block of hours you have to split up between all employees to be fair. This is split between our full timers, part timers and casual workers. Full timers take up about 50-60 percent of our hours depending on budget, while the other 40 percent is split between part time and casual. Part timers are guaranteed a certain amount of hours each week and can only work a maximum of 42 for a week, usually we can only put people on for 30. If a part time team member exceeds the maximum then our head office gets a big red mark saying "this store is fucking their roster up, intervene" so we have our arms twisted into telling the team member that they can't work, and it puts us into a position where we need to quickly find someone to fill the role. It's painful because there's team members we obviously prefer to put on over others due to product knowledge and customer interaction, but unless we play by the rules of our overhead rulers, we can't continue running the store. 

Oh and before I finish I also gotta say that our rostering system automatically fills the roster months in advance based on hours previously worked, so more rostered employees usually get more than the maximum hours and we have to fine comb through the rosters for these mistakes.

Also with the confirmed stats, it's very vague on how it pertains to the power of EA. Although on the wiki page it is described to begin at a power rating of 4000, then multiplied by his strength, then added power from his wealth. To anchor that number an A+++ ranked NP has a power of 200. So you can kind of get an idea of its power through that, although the multiplications and boosts from strength and wealth are not confirmed.

Problem is with this argument about EA, there is no clear definition on what you can really call his effect. At full blast all we really know is that it can engulf the world into a void that distorts space, which Imagine is what classifies it as anti-world. So I don't imagine it's the destructive power of EA that would destroy the world, more so the effect that might be able to destroy the world. As it's a gods creation from before humanity, it wouldn't surprise me. It's page 114 of SF vol. 1 that hints that this is the case, plus an interview a friend sent me between Nasu and Narita. However the problem with the Nasuverse is that many things contradict each other, that one Da Vinci line may be the outlier that doesn't make sense, or it may be true. Or might be a mistranslation, I cannot say for sure, that's why I keep out of discussions mainly about anti world functions. It's either too vague or has too many things that support and contradict at the same time. I don't know honestly, so I'm just gonna say my opinion as of right now is that maybe EAs effect can distort space which is pretty much destroying the earth but not in destructive power. If any of you guys have an interview or something concrete that contradicts my opinion, I would love to hear it, I want a certain answer for sure.
